- Organism: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (strain ATCC 25618 / H37Rv)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=29.3%, query coverage=50.8%, target coverage=57.2%, E-value=1.76e-15
- function: Required for host-cell death and may support an EsxA-independent virulence function (PubMed:23869560). Secreted processed form of EspB binds to phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylserine (PubMed:23869560). Inhibits IFN-gamma-induced autophagy in murine macrophages (PubMed:25641595).

- subunit: Mature EspB oligomerizes and forms donut-shaped rings. In contrast, the full-length protein does not oligomerize (PubMed:26051906). Interacts with the C-terminal region of EspK (PubMed:17676952).

entities.name: EspB query protein
observations: 526 aa protein; exact sequence hash match to curated Mycolicibacterium smegmatis EspB accession L8FKX3.
Contains EspB_PE domain PF18625.9 at residues 12-84 and EspB_PPE domain PF21856.3 at residues 135-282.
Curated homolog annotation indicates secretion through the ESX-1/type VII secretion system and extracellular localization.
Sequence is acidic overall (theoretical pI 4.73; predicted charge at pH 7 approximately -27.6) and contains extensive glycine/proline-rich low-complexity regions, especially in the C-terminal half.
No sequence-derived evidence in the supplied analysis for a conventional signal peptide or transmembrane helix; ESX-1 secretion is therefore the relevant export mechanism rather than Sec/Tat export.

observations: EspB is a secreted ESX-1/type VII secretion-associated protein.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis EspB has a curated extracellular localization annotation and forms oligomeric donut-shaped rings after processing; these detailed mechanistic findings are homolog-based and may not apply identically to every EspB ortholog.
